properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 6 at 3:52AM CDT until October 6 at 6:45AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Cameron County in deep south Texas...
Southeastern Willacy County in deep south Texas...

* WHEN...Until 645 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 352 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 0.5 and 1.3 inches of rain has fallen in the past hour.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Los Fresnos, South Padre Island, Rancho Viejo, Rio Hondo,
Laureles, Port Of Brownsville, Olmito, Cameron Park, Arroyo City,
Southmost, Downtown Brownsville, Brownsville, Lincoln Park, Holly
Beach, Laguna Vista Police Department, Palmer Laasko Elementary,
Los Fresnos High School, Los Fresnos City Offices, Laguna Heights
and Lopez - Riggins Elementary School.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 6 at 1:27AM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from this afternoon
through Friday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6
AM Wednesday to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Minor coastal erosion is also
expected. Additionally, elevated surf will lead to strong rip
currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-5 feet, with sets to 6
feet, on south- and southwest-facing beaches. High tides are
expected to peak between 6.5 and 7.0 feet during the mornings
and evenings.
properties.instruction:
A beach hazards statement for elevated surf means that waves will
be high enough to cause danger to inexperienced swimmers in the
water. Elevated surf also frequently results in strong rip
currents which can drag people away from the shore and possibly
result in drowning. Always swim near a lifeguard.

A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that tides and elevated surf
will combine to generate localized flooding of low areas along the
shore.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 6 at 1:09AM PDT until October 8 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the mid-90s to
near 105. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will
limit overnight relief.

* WHERE...The East Bay and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, North Bay
Interior Mountains and Valleys, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern
Hills, The Santa Cruz Mountains, Interior Monterey County and the
Santa Lucia Range, Most of San Benito County and the Cholame Hills
in Southeast Monterey County, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo
Seco and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...For the Heat Advisory, this level of heat affects anyone
without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely
in some health systems, heat-sensitive industries and
infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 6 at 2:48AM CDT until October 6 at 4:45AM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 445 AM CDT.

* At 248 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 24 nm southeast of Okaloosa Deep Water
Reef, or 29 nm southwest of Panama City Beach. The severe
thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
